remaining_concerns: The affected public benefits eligibility segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The segment is below target on residency documentation guidance.
The available risk-acceptance draft is not approved.
The draft does not address the public benefits eligibility exposure.
Policy says rollout controls and small-percentage launch do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
There is no admissible evidence that the required pre-launch model-card disclosure has actually been completed or approved.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the core unresolved predicates. The response narrows the certification theory to a caveated position, but that is still a reinterpretation of the same record, not proof that the policy condition has been satisfied. The admissible evidence still shows: the named public-benefits eligibility use case remains exposed; that segment is below target; rollout is limited and reversible but does not exclude the affected use case; the only risk-acceptance artifact is unapproved and does not cover this exposure; and policy requires disclosure unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Because there is still no admissible evidence that the required pre-launch disclosure has actually been completed or approved, the compliance predicate remains open. That distinction matters: a caveated path might become supportable if disclosure were evidenced, but agreement that disclosure is required is not itself evidence that disclosure occurred.
